request: Add two click buttons with the height of 2 millimetre to provide a comfortable and responsive feel for the user

parameters.height_reference: Measure 2 millimetres outward from the underlying upper crown surface along the local surface-normal direction
parameters.button_arrangement: One left primary button and one right secondary button
parameters.placement: Upper finger-contact region of the housing, positioned bilaterally on the two sides of the scroll-wheel support pedestal
parameters.symmetry: Use the longitudinal vertical center plane as the nominal symmetry reference while accommodating the model's slight geometric asymmetry
parameters.construction: Create two distinct button-cap sections rather than merging them permanently into the upper shell
parameters.edge_treatment: Apply small comfort fillets or chamfers without reducing the required 2 millimetre nominal button height

actions.target: The upper ergonomic shell surrounding the scroll wheel is the functional and geometric host. Localize both new click buttons on the upward-facing crown surface, with one button on each side of the central scroll-wheel pedestal. The buttons should occupy the forward and central finger-contact portion of the crown rather than the rounded rear palm-support region.
actions.relational_constraint: The specified height applies to each click button. Both buttons must follow the curvature and longitudinal slope of the upper crown, remain separated from each other by a center clearance corridor around the scroll-wheel support pedestal, and preserve unobstructed rotation and access to the scroll wheel. Their outer boundaries must remain inset from the left flank, right flank, and tapered front-nose transitions. The two button caps should be approximately bilateral about the housing center plane and should have comparable visible area and travel behavior.
actions.unresolved_reference: The request does not specify the button planform, perimeter gap, actuation travel, hinge or pivot arrangement, switch position, wall thickness, minimum clearance from the wheel, or manufacturing process. These values must be selected from product-design standards or provided before production release. The 2 millimetre value is interpreted as the nominal protrusion of each button cap above the existing crown, not as shell thickness or click travel.
steps: Use Section S01, the Upper ergonomic shell, as the host section. Select face code 0000, Brep_id FACE 6, identified as the large upward-facing B-spline crown surrounding the wheel-support interface.

Do not place the buttons on S02 because the lower base is not a user click surface, or on S03 because the peripheral side and end shell primarily forms the grip and structural perimeter. Preserve S03 faces 0003 and 0005 as uninterrupted left and right gripping flanks and preserve face 0004 at the tapered front nose.

Treat S04 and S05 as protected reference geometry. Use the scroll-wheel support pedestal and the wheel centerline to establish button placement, but do not modify pedestal faces 0006 through 0010 or wheel faces 0011 through 0014.

Create or identify the longitudinal vertical center datum plane passing through the scroll wheel and the approximate bilateral center of the housing. Use the transverse axis of S05 and the rectangular opening or interface of S04 as secondary references for locating this plane.

Generate a tangent or best-fit construction plane over the central-forward portion of face 0000. Orient its longitudinal direction from the low tapered front nose toward the high rounded rear heel and orient its transverse direction from the left flank toward the right flank.

Project the visible outer boundary of face 0000, the rectangular wheel-pedestal interface, and the center plane into the layout sketch. These projected entities are construction references and must not be used to alter the wheel or pedestal.

Define a protected central corridor around S04 and S05. Offset the projected pedestal boundary sufficiently to provide assembly, rotation, and finger-access clearance. Keep both button profiles outside this corridor so neither button can interfere with the wheel tread during full button travel.

Sketch the left button planform on the left side of the center corridor. Use a smooth ergonomic outline extending through the forward and central finger-contact region of the crown. Keep its outside edge inset from the transition between face 0000 and the left flank face 0003, and keep its forward edge inset from the transition to the tapered front nose face 0004.

Create the right button profile by mirroring the nominal left profile about the longitudinal center plane. Because the housing is only approximately symmetric, adapt or trim the mirrored profile to remain properly inset from the right flank face 0005 and to follow the actual boundary of face 0000.

Use split-face, wrap, or project-to-surface functionality to map both planar profiles onto the B-spline crown. This produces button boundaries that conform to the existing double curvature and sloped top profile rather than remaining flat in global space.

Copy or offset the bounded crown patches corresponding to the left and right button footprints. Preserve the local curvature of face 0000 so the completed buttons visually continue the ergonomic shell form.

Offset each button patch outward by 2 millimetres along its local surface normals. Where a direct surface offset is unstable, construct each cap with boundary surfaces or a loft between the original mapped perimeter and the 2 millimetre offset perimeter, while maintaining the nominal 2 millimetre crown-to-cap height.

Close the sidewalls of each offset patch to create two watertight button-cap solids or manufacturable surface bodies. Keep the left and right caps as separate new sections so they can move independently and actuate separate click mechanisms.

Introduce a narrow perimeter clearance or reveal between each cap and the underlying upper shell as required for button travel. If the model represents a production enclosure, split or cut face 0000 along the mapped profiles and create recessed seats below the caps; do not cut through the protected pedestal interface.

If a rear-hinged mouse-button behavior is intended, retain or create a compliant attachment zone toward the rear edge of each cap and leave the forward and side edges free for downward actuation. If discrete mechanical switches are intended instead, add underside actuator bosses aligned with the future switch locations after internal component coordinates are supplied.

Blend the exposed upper perimeter of each button with small tangent fillets suitable for fingertip comfort. Apply a small chamfer or fillet to lower side edges to remove sharp edges while preserving the specified 2 millimetre nominal protrusion at the principal finger-contact surface.

Check the side views to confirm that the new caps follow the low-to-high longitudinal slope of the existing shell and do not create abrupt steps into the rounded rear palm-support crown. Check the front and back views to confirm comparable left and right elevations.

Perform interference and clearance checks against S04 and S05 through the full proposed button travel. Verify that the wheel can rotate about its transverse axis and that neither cap, cap sidewall, nor reveal enters the pedestal volume.

Verify that the new profiles do not intersect the outer perimeter faces of S03 and that sufficient material remains in face 0000 between the button openings, wheel-pedestal interface, and shell boundary to carry click loads into the sidewalls.

Validate the final model as the original housing solid, the original separate scroll-wheel solid, and two newly created click-button sections. Recalculate visual face codes and Brep face indices after regeneration because the split crown and newly created cap faces will receive new identifiers.

intention: Provide a comfortable and responsive feel for the user
